label: British Vernacular Architecture
defn: the traditional houses and farm buildings of Britain and Ireland in local materials, studied by regional type and by framing and walling tradition: Wealden hall houses, cruck-framed halls, Devon cob, Hebridean blackhouses, Dartmoor longhouses, border bastles.
aliases: vernacular architecture of Britain;English vernacular architecture;British vernacular building
see: K5-1 Tudor Architecture; K2-7 Tudor Revival Architecture; K6-1 Arts and Crafts Architecture.
note: Possession hand-off P0451 (G2 Wealden hall house)

label: German Vernacular Architecture
defn: the traditional timber-framed (Fachwerk) and log-and-frame houses and farmhouses of the German-speaking lands, studied by regional house type: the Low German hall house, the Black Forest house, the Umgebinde house of Upper Lusatia, half-timbered towns such as Quedlinburg.
see: K5-22 Renaissance Architecture (Weser Renaissance); K6-11 Reform Architecture.

label: Kulla
defn: the fortified stone tower house of Albania and Kosovo (17th–19th century), with a stone ground floor and a timber-galleried upper oda: Kulla of Mazrek (Junik), the kullas of Dukagjin and Gjirokastër.
see: K12-11 Vainakh Tower Architecture; K1-12 Ottoman Architecture.

label: Vainakh Tower Architecture
defn: the stone residential and battle towers of the Chechens and Ingush in the North Caucasus (11th–18th century), the battle towers with stepped pyramidal roofs: Vovnushki, Erzi, Nikaroy.
see: K4-6 Architecture of Georgia; K12-10 Kulla.
note: Possession hand-off P0460 (G2 Vainakh tower building)

label: Spanish Vernacular Architecture
defn: the traditional rural houses of Spain in their regional types and materials: the Catalan masia, the Cantabrian casona and casa montañesa, the Basque and Navarrese casa torre and caserío.
see: K1-5 Mudéjar Architecture; K2-17 Eclecticism in Architecture (Neo-Basque style).

label: Italian Vernacular Architecture
defn: the traditional rural building of Italy and its islands in local stone and earth: the corbelled dry-stone trulli of Apulia, the domed dammusi of Pantelleria.

label: American Vernacular Architecture
defn: the folk and vernacular house types of the United States, classified by plan and massing rather than by style: the shotgun house, the I-house, the upright-and-wing house, the New England connected farm, the Charleston single house.
aliases: American folk architecture;vernacular architecture of the United States;American folk house
see: K5-15 American Colonial Architecture; K5-19 French Colonial Architecture; K2-18 Victorian Architecture.

label: Malay Traditional House
defn: the stilted timber house of the Malay world, joined without nails, with steep thatched or tiled roofs and carved panels, in regional types: rumah limas, rumah bumbung panjang, Minangkabau rumah gadang.
see: I1-9 Malay Woodcarving; K9-10 Batak Architecture.
note: Possession hand-off P0473 (G2 Malay timber house)

label: Haveli
defn: the courtyard townhouse and mansion of north India and Pakistan, inward-looking round one or more chowks, with carved jharokhas and often painted walls: the havelis of Shekhawati, Jaisalmer's Patwon ki Haveli, Old Delhi and Lahore havelis.
see: K7-14 Rajput Architecture; L2-8 Shekhawati Frescoes.

label: Nordic Log Architecture
defn: the notched solid-log building tradition of Scandinavia and Finland for houses, farm buildings and churches: Norwegian lofts and stabbur, Swedish timmerhus, Finnish hirsitalo farmhouses.
see: K2-30 National Romantic Style; K2-32 Swiss Chalet Style.
note: Possession hand-off P0476 (G2 Finnish log-house building)

label: Kashmiri Houseboat
defn: the moored cedar houseboat of Srinagar's Dal and Nageen lakes (from the early 1900s), built and run by the Hanji, with carved walnut panelling and khatamband ceilings.
note: Possession hand-off P0477 (G2 Kashmiri houseboat building)

label: Swiss Farmhouse Architecture
defn: the traditional timber farmhouses of Switzerland in their regional types, the vernacular source of the chalet: the Frutighaus of the Bernese Oberland, the Bernese Mittelland house, the Appenzell house.

label: French Vernacular Architecture
defn: the traditional rural houses of France in their regional types: the longère of Brittany and Normandy, the mas of Provence, the Basque etxe.

label: Cycladic Architecture
defn: the whitewashed cubic stone houses, chapels and windmills of the Cyclades, flat-roofed and set in dense hill villages: Oia (Santorini), Chora (Mykonos), Kastro (Sifnos).

label: Chattel House
defn: the small movable timber house of Barbados, built on loose stone blocks without nails so tenants could dismantle it, with gabled roof and fretwork trim: Tyrol Cot Heritage Village.

label: Assam-type House
defn: the light timber- or bamboo-framed house of Assam and north-east India (late 19th–20th century), on a raised plinth with steep roof and wide veranda, built for monsoon and earthquake: bungalows of Shillong and Guwahati.

label: Queenslander
defn: the timber house of Queensland raised on stumps, with corrugated-iron roof and deep verandas, built from the 1840s to today: workers' cottages and high-set houses of Brisbane's inner suburbs.
see: K2-33 Federation Architecture; K2-18 Victorian Architecture.

label: Bonsai
defn: the Japanese art of the trained miniature tree in a container, shaped by pruning and wiring into named styles and size classes and shown in alcove display: Ōmiya Bonsai Village, the Kokufu-ten exhibition, saikei tray landscapes.

label: Penjing
defn: the Chinese art of miniature trees and landscapes in containers (from the Tang dynasty), in tree, rock-landscape and water-and-land forms and regional schools, precursor of bonsai: Lingnan, Shanghai, Yangzhou, Suzhou and Sichuan penjing.
see: K14-1 Bonsai; K14-3 Hòn Non Bộ; K13-3 Chinese Garden.

label: Hòn Non Bộ
defn: the Vietnamese art of miniature rock landscapes of islands and mountains set in water with plants, viewed from all sides (from the 10th century).
note: Possession hand-off P0655 (C3 Hòn non bộ)

label: Ikebana
defn: the Japanese art of flower arrangement (kadō), from Buddhist altar offerings to the schools that codified its forms: Ikenobō rikka and shōka, Ohara moribana, Sōgetsu free style.
aliases: kadō;way of the flower;Japanese flower arrangement

label: Turkish Mosaic Lamp
defn: the Turkish craft of covering blown-glass lamp globes with small hand-cut pieces of coloured glass and beads set in grout, made in Istanbul and Cappadocia for the bazaar trade: hanging mosaic lamps, table lamps.
note: Possession hand-off P0129 (B3 Turkish mosaic lamp making); attestation rests on a seller or craft blog

label: Swedish Art Glass
defn: the art glass of the Småland glassworks from the 1910s, where artists such as Simon Gate, Edward Hald, Edvin Öhrström and Vicke Lindstrand designed for Orrefors and Kosta, with cased and encased techniques of their own: Graal and Ariel vases, engraved Orrefors bowls.
aliases: Orrefors glass;Kosta glass;Kingdom of Crystal;Swedish Modern glass
see: F2-2 Bohemian Glass; F1-10 Studio Glass; I3-16 Art Deco.
note: Possession hand-off P0134 (B4 Swedish art glass)

label: Lauscha Glass
defn: the lamp-blown and mould-blown glass of Lauscha in Thuringia (from the 16th century), silvered inside and hand-painted, where the glass Christmas bauble originated and was exported worldwide from the 1840s: blown baubles, figural ornaments, glass eyes and marbles.
aliases: Lauschaer Glas;Lauscha glass ornaments;Thuringian glass Christmas ornaments
see: F1-7 Czech Blown Glass Bead Christmas Decorations.
note: Possession hand-off P0138 (B4 Lauscha glass ornaments)

label: Garden Gnomes
defn: moulded and hand-painted terracotta garden figures of bearded dwarfs made in Gräfenroda, Thuringia, from the 1870s by Philipp Griebel and others, later copied worldwide: Griebel gnomes, Heissner gnomes.
note: Possession hand-off P0146 (B4 Thuringian garden gnomes)

label: Edo Glass
defn: the hand-blown and lampworked glass of Tokyo from the late Edo period, a designated traditional craft (Edo garasu): inside-painted Edo fūrin wind bells, Sasaki-type glass pens.

label: Banko Ware
defn: stoneware of Yokkaichi in Mie, founded by Nunami Rōzan in the 18th century and refounded in the Meiji era, its petalite-rich body resisting flame: donabe casseroles, purple-clay kyūsu teapots.
see: E3-20 Iga Ware; E3-22 Tokoname Ware.

label: Hasami Ware
defn: porcelain of Hasami in Hizen (Nagasaki) from 1599, a sister of Arita that became Japan's largest maker of everyday blue-and-white and celadon: kurawanka bowls, konpira bottles.
see: E4-16 Arita Ware; E4-19 Hirado Ware.

label: Mino Ware
defn: the stoneware and porcelain of the Mino kilns in Gifu (Tajimi, Toki, Mizunami, Kani), from medieval ash-glazed wares to the Momoyama tea wares and the largest modern Japanese production; its named tea wares Shino and Oribe are their own leaves: Ki-Seto, Setoguro, Mino-Iga.
see: E3-16 Shino Ware; E3-17 Oribe Ware; E3-15 Seto Ware.

label: Edo Kiriko
defn: the cut glass of Tokyo founded by Kagaya Kyūbei in 1834, clear or colour-cased glass wheel-cut in fine geometric patterns (yarai, kiku-tsunagi, nanako): cased sake cups, cut tumblers.
see: F2-2 Bohemian Glass; F1-14 Edo Glass.

label: Impruneta Terracotta
defn: the unglazed, iron-rich terracotta of Impruneta south of Florence, made since the 14th century by hand and coiling: large orange-tree pots of the Boboli Gardens, basins, cotto floor tiles and bricks.

label: Thrapsano Pottery
defn: the village pottery of Thrapsano in central Crete, of Minoan descent, where teams threw large storage jars on the wheel, travelling on summer campaigns (ventema): pitharia storage jars.

label: Encaustic Tiles
defn: earthenware floor tiles with a pattern inlaid in contrasting clay, made in medieval England and France (13th–16th century) and revived industrially in the Gothic Revival by Minton, Maw & Co and Craven Dunnill (c. 1840–1930s): Chertsey Abbey tiles, Palace of Westminster floors.
aliases: inlaid tiles;Victorian encaustic tiles;medieval inlaid floor tiles
see: E1-79 Staffordshire Pottery; I3-13 Victorian Decorative Arts.
note: Possession hand-off P0253 (C8 Victorian encaustic tile)

label: Roman Micromosaic
defn: pictures and jewellery made of minute pulled-glass (smalti filati) tesserae in Rome from the late 18th century, led by the Vatican Mosaic Studio and sold on the Grand Tour: micromosaic plaques of Roman views, snuff-box lids, brooches.
see: D3-10 Pietra Dura; L3-8 Byzantine Mosaics.

label: Kachelofen
defn: the glazed relief and painted stove tiles (Ofenkacheln) and tiled stoves of the German-speaking lands and Scandinavia, built by the Hafner (stove-fitter potter) trade from the late Middle Ages: Renaissance relief-tile stoves, Effner's Schleissheim stove, Swedish kakelugn.
note: Possession hand-off P0536 (G3 Kachelofen (German and Austrian tiled stove))

label: Egyptian Hand-Blown Glass
defn: the free-blown glass of Cairo's workshops, including recycled Muski glass and the decorative bottles of the Khan el-Khalili perfume trade: perfume-oil bottles, Muski tumblers.
see: F1-2 Syrian Glassblowing; F3-1 Mamluk Enamelled Glass.
note: Possession hand-off P0547 (H4 Egyptian hand-blown perfume glass); attestation rests on a seller or craft blog

label: Torre del Greco Shell and Coral Carving
defn: the carving of shell cameos and Mediterranean coral at Torre del Greco near Naples from the 17th century, cut with the bulino scraper: sardonyx-shell cameo brooches, carved coral branches and beads.
aliases: Torre del Greco cameos;shell cameo carving;Neapolitan coral carving
note: Possession hand-off P0014 (A3 Torre del Greco shell and coral carving)

label: Temple Jewellery
defn: gold jewellery set with red and green stones, first made to adorn the deities of South Indian temples and now worn by brides and Bharatanatyam dancers, centred on Nagercoil (GI): jhumka, oddiyanam waist belts, nethi chutti.
aliases: temple jewellery of Nagercoil;Nagercoil temple jewellery
see: G3-2 Mughal Jewellery; D5-5 Chola Bronzes.
note: Possession hand-off P0022 (A3 Temple jewellery of Nagercoil)

label: Thewa
defn: the Rajput craft of Pratapgarh in Rajasthan, from the 18th century, of fusing finely chased 23-carat gold sheet onto coloured glass: pendants, jewellery boxes, plaques with hunting and Krishna scenes.

label: Tarakasi
defn: the silver filigree of Cuttack in Odisha, of fine drawn wire shaped and soldered by hand: filigree ornaments, brooches, temple decorations for Durga Puja.
see: G3-1 Fatimid Jewellery; G1-38 Kubachi Silver.

label: Hopi Silverwork
defn: silver jewellery of Hopi smiths, from the late 1930s worked in the overlay technique developed with the Museum of Northern Arizona, a cut-out top sheet soldered over a darkened base: overlay bracelets, belt buckles, bolo ties.
see: G3-15 Navajo Silverwork; G3-16 Zuni Jewelry.

label: Taxco Silver
defn: the silver jewellery and silverware of Taxco in Guerrero, revived from 1931 by William Spratling's workshops and carried on by his pupils: Los Castillo, Antonio Pineda, Hector Aguilar.

label: Jura Watchmaking
defn: mechanical watchmaking and art mechanics (automata, music boxes) of the Franco-Swiss Jura arc and Geneva, 17th century to the present, with engraved and gilt movements, enamelled cases and painted dials; inscribed by UNESCO in 2020: Geneva enamel watches, Jura complications, automata.
aliases: Swiss watchmaking;Geneva watchmaking;craftsmanship of mechanical watchmaking and art mechanics
note: Possession hand-off P0049 (A5 Swiss and French Jura watchmaking)

label: Black Forest Clockmaking
defn: cottage and factory clocks of Triberg and Furtwangen, mid-17th c.–present, with painted shield dials and carved cuckoo-clock cases.
note: Possession hand-off P0050 (A5 Black Forest clockmaking)

label: London Clockmaking
defn: london clocks of c. 1660–1800 (Knibb, Tompion, Quare): ebony and marquetry longcase and bracket clocks, engraved backplates.
note: Possession hand-off P0051 (A5 English clockmaking (London school))

label: Glashütte Watchmaking
defn: saxon watchmaking of Glashütte from A. Lange's 1845 workshop, with three-quarter plates and hand-engraved balance cocks.

label: Comtoise Clockmaking
defn: provincial French longcase clocks of Franche-Comté (Morbier, Morez), 1680–c. 1910, with embossed brass lyre pendulums and painted cases.

label: Mora Clockmaking
defn: swedish longcase clocks of Mora in Dalarna, late 18th–19th c., cottage movements in painted, waisted pine cases.

label: Wadokei
defn: japanese clocks of the Edo period showing unequal temporal hours: pillar, pillow and bracket clocks in lacquered and engraved cases.
see: I2-10 Japanese Lacquerware; G2-4 Japanese Sword Mountings.
note: Possession hand-off P0055 (A5 Japanese wadokei clockmaking)

label: Vienna Regulator Clockmaking
defn: weight-driven precision wall clocks of Vienna, c. 1780–1930, in glazed Biedermeier and later historicist cases.
note: Possession hand-off P0056 (A5 Vienna regulator clockmaking)

label: Connecticut Clockmaking
defn: mass-produced shelf clocks of Connecticut from Eli Terry (c. 1814): pillar-and-scroll and OG cases with reverse-painted glass tablets.
note: Possession hand-off P0057 (A5 American clock industry (Connecticut))

label: Moroccan Metalwork
defn: the brass and copper work of Fez, Marrakesh and Meknes, pierced, chased and worked in repoussé with geometric and floral openwork: pierced lanterns set with coloured glass, trays, incense burners.
note: Possession hand-off P0130 (B3 Moroccan pierced brass lanterns)

label: Nanbu Tekki
defn: cast iron of the old Nanbu domain (Morioka and Mizusawa, Iwate) from the 17th century, sand-cast with arare hailstone and relief patterns: tetsubin kettles, chagama tea kettles, furin wind bells.

label: Solingen Cutlery
defn: blades of the Klingenstadt Solingen, medieval–present: etched sword blades, then knives, scissors and razors.

label: Thiers Cutlery
defn: cutlery of Thiers on the Durolle, documented from the 13th c., France's main knife centre (Sabatier, Laguiole makers).

label: Uchihamono
defn: Japanese forged blades, steel forge-welded to soft iron, clay-quenched and hand-sharpened, made in centres designated as traditional crafts: Sakai, Echizen, Tosa, Banshu Miki and Echigo Sanjo uchihamono.
see: G2-3 Japanese Swords; G1-61 Solingen Cutlery.

label: Sheffield Cutlery
defn: cutlery of Sheffield under the Cutlers' Company of Hallamshire (1624), with crucible steel (1740s) and pearl and ivory handles.

label: Longquan Swords
defn: swords forged at Longquan in Zhejiang, by tradition from the smith Ou Yezi, with folded steel and fittings in brass and rayskin (national ICH 2006): jian, dao.

label: Khukuri
defn: the forward-curving chopping knife of Nepal, forged with fullers and carried in sheaths with chased silver chapes, the weapon of the Gurkhas: Ang Khola, Dui Chira, ceremonial silver-mounted khukuris.
see: G2-6 Puukko; G2-1 Islamic Arms and Armour.
note: Possession hand-off P0333 (E4 Nepali khukuri smithing)

label: Yumi
defn: the tall asymmetrical Japanese bow laminated from bamboo and wood, made by bowyers (yumi-shi) for archery and kyūdō: Miyakonojō daikyū, lacquered and rattan-bound Edo bows.
see: G2-12 Japanese Armour; G2-3 Japanese Swords.
note: Possession hand-off P0334 (E4 Miyakonojō bamboo bow-making)

label: Gakgung
defn: the Korean composite horn bow of horn, bamboo and sinew glued with isinglass and covered in birch bark, Joseon period to the present; its makers designated gungsi (1971).
note: Possession hand-off P0335 (E4 Korean gakgung bow-making)

label: German Gothic Armour
defn: south German plate armour of c. 1420–1530 from Augsburg, Nuremberg, Landshut and Innsbruck, with fluted, cusped and etched plates, passing into the Maximilian style: Gothic harnesses, sallets, Maximilian fluted armour.
note: Possession hand-off P0337 (E4 German Gothic armouring)

label: Japanese Armour
defn: samurai armour of laced lacquered scales and plates from the Heian to the Edo period, with helmets and face masks by armourer schools such as the Myōchin: ō-yoroi, dō-maru, tōsei gusoku, kabuto, menpō.
see: G2-3 Japanese Swords; G2-4 Japanese Sword Mountings; I2 Lacquer.

label: European Scientific Instruments
defn: mathematical, optical and philosophical instruments of Europe from the Renaissance to the 19th century, of engraved and lacquered brass in veneered cases, made by named workshops: Latin astrolabes, London telescopes and microscopes, wheel barometers.
note: Possession hand-off P0339 (E6 English barometer making)

label: Bezalel School
defn: the style of the Bezalel School of Arts and Crafts in Jerusalem (from 1906), founded by Boris Schatz to create a Jewish national art, its workshops of Yemenite Jewish silversmiths making filigree Judaica: Hanukkah lamps, Torah ornaments, spice boxes, Bezalel carpets.
aliases: Bezalel style;Bezalel School of Arts and Crafts
see: I3-14 Arts and Crafts Movement; I3-15 Art Nouveau.

label: Nachiarkoil Lamps
defn: hollow-cast brass lamps made since 1857 by Kammalar families at Nachiarkoil in Tamil Nadu in river-sand moulds (GI 2010): kuthuvilakku standing lamps, annam swan lamps.

label: Oil-Paper Umbrella
defn: the craft of bamboo-ribbed umbrellas covered in hand-made paper, waterproofed with tung or persimmon oil and painted with flowers, birds and calligraphy, from China to Japan and Southeast Asia: Luzhou and Meinong oil-paper umbrellas, Japanese wagasa, Pathein umbrellas.
see: C4 Paper Arts; C4-8 Fan Making.
note: Possession hand-off P0037 (A4 Chinese oil-paper umbrella)

label: Fan Making
defn: the making and painting of hand fans, folding and flat, in paper, silk, bamboo, ivory and lacquer, studied as decorated objects with named centres: Kyoto sensu and uchiwa, Hangzhou folding fans, Valencian painted fans, Parisian éventails.
see: A2 (fan painting is a format tag); I2 Lacquer.
note: Possession hand-off P0044 (A4 Valencian fan making)

label: Chōchin
defn: the Japanese craft of collapsible paper lanterns of washi stretched over a spiral split-bamboo frame, painted or lettered with crests and scenes, in named centres: Gifu chōchin, Odawara chōchin, Mito chōchin.
note: Possession hand-off P0128 (B3 Japanese chōchin lantern making)

label: Inkstone Carving
defn: the carving of inkstones from fine-grained stone, graded by quarry and decorated in relief with landscapes, dragons and inscriptions, collected as scholar's objects in China and Japan: Duan inkstones of Zhaoqing, She inkstones of Wuyuan, Amehata suzuri.
see: C1-9 Chinese Calligraphy; D3-4 Chinese Snuff Bottles.
note: Possession hand-off P0237 (C5 Duan inkstone carving)

label: East Asian Bookbinding
defn: the book forms of China, Korea, Japan and Vietnam, from scrolls, concertina and butterfly bindings to side-stitched thread binding (xianzhuang) of folded leaves in cloth cases: Ming and Qing xianzhuang books, Japanese fukuro-toji wahon, Korean five-hole bindings.
see: C3-3 Fine Binding; C2-12 Sutra Copying.
note: Possession hand-off P0350 (F1 Chinese thread binding)

label: Volterra Alabaster Carving
defn: the carving and turning of local alabaster at Volterra in Tuscany, revived in the 18th century after the Etruscan urns, in vases, busts, figures and ornament by named workshops: Inghirami workshop, Società Cooperativa Artieri dell'Alabastro.

label: Korean Calligraphy
defn: seoye: the Korean art of the brush in Hanja and Hangul, from Silla and Goryeo masters to the Joseon court and the Chusa style of Kim Jeong-hui: Kim Saeng's works, Han Ho's Seokbong style, Kim Jeong-hui's Chusa-che.
see: C1-9 Chinese Calligraphy; C1-10 Japanese Calligraphy.

label: Scherenschnitte
defn: the scissor-cut paper silhouettes and pictures of German-speaking Switzerland and Germany, carried by Pennsylvania Germans to America in the 18th century: Pays-d'Enhaut alpine cuts, Johann Jakob Hauswirth, Pennsylvania German love letters.
see: C4-3 Chinese Paper Cutting; C2-28 Fraktur.

label: Kirie
defn: Japanese paper-cut pictures, cut with a knife from black or coloured paper, often backed with colour, from Edo katagami practice to modern kirie artists.
see: C4-3 Chinese Paper Cutting; H5-19 Katazome.

label: Wycinanki
defn: Polish folk paper cutting in bright layered colours, made for cottage walls and festivals in named regional styles: Łowicz layered cuts, Kurpie single-colour leluje.

label: Idar-Oberstein Agate Cutting
defn: the cutting, carving and engraving of agate, jasper and gemstones at Idar-Oberstein on the Nahe from the 15th century, later on Brazilian agate: carved agate bowls, animal sculptures, cameos.
see: D3-7 Engraved Gems; D3-10 Pietra Dura.
note: Possession hand-off P0437 (F6 Idar-Oberstein agate cutting)

label: Taxidermy
defn: mounted animal skins made as displays to be looked at, from the glass-case birds and domes of the Victorian parlour to the anthropomorphic tableaux of Walter Potter (Bramber) and the trophy studios of Rowland Ward (London) and Van Ingen & Van Ingen (Mysore).

label: Meerschaum Carving
defn: the carving of sepiolite (meerschaum) into figural and ornamented pipe bowls and objects, from 18th-century Vienna to the Eskişehir workshops of Turkey: Eskişehir lületaşı pipes, Viennese figural pipes.
note: Possession hand-off P0550 (J10 Eskişehir meerschaum carving)

label: Aran Knitting
defn: the cabled hand-knitting of the Aran Islands off Co. Galway, worked in undyed báinín wool with cable, honeycomb, diamond and moss stitches, exported worldwide from the 1950s: Aran jumpers, geansaí Árann.
see: H4-95 Gansey Knitting; H4-83 Orenburg Shawl.

label: Gansey Knitting
defn: the close-knit seaman's jumpers of Guernsey and the British fishing coasts, knitted in the round in worsted with underarm gussets and textured yoke patterns that vary by village: Guernsey frocks, Filey and Cornish ganseys.
note: Possession hand-off P0556 (A1 Guernsey and gansey knitting)

label: Fair Isle Knitting
defn: stranded two-colour knitting of Fair Isle and Shetland, worked in the round in short floats with OXO and star bands, fashionable from 1921: Fair Isle jumpers, Shetland yoke sweaters.
note: Possession hand-off P0557 (A1 Fair Isle and Shetland knitting)

label: Lopapeysa
defn: the Icelandic yoke sweater knitted seamless in unspun lopi wool with a patterned circular yoke, a national symbol since the mid-20th century.
see: H4-96 Fair Isle Knitting; H4-98 Norwegian Knitting.
note: Possession hand-off P0558 (A1 Icelandic lopapeysa knitting)

label: Norwegian Knitting
defn: the regional two-colour stranded knitting of Norway, with lice stitches and embroidered bands: Setesdal lusekofte, Fana cardigans, Selbu mittens and the Selbu rose, and their 20th-century descendants.
see: H7-5 Bunad; H4-96 Fair Isle Knitting.
note: Possession hand-off P0559 (A1 Norwegian colourwork knitting)

label: Cowichan Knitting
defn: the heavy shawl-collar sweaters hand-knitted by Coast Salish women of the Cowichan Valley on Vancouver Island in hand-spun undyed wool with pictorial motifs, from the late 19th century.

label: Basotho Blanket
defn: the woollen blankets worn as cloaks by the Basotho of Lesotho and South Africa since the 1870s, whose named designs and pin-stripes mark rank, marriage and initiation: seanamarena, Victoria England, letlama.

label: Sukajan
defn: the densely embroidered souvenir jackets born around the US naval base at Yokosuka after 1945, their dragons, tigers and eagles worked by kimono embroiderers of Kiryū and Ashikaga.
note: Possession hand-off P0568 (A1 Yokosuka sukajan embroidery)

label: Savile Row Tailoring
defn: the bespoke men's tailoring of Savile Row in London from the early 19th century, cut from a pattern drafted for each client and the model of the structured English suit: Henry Poole, Huntsman, Anderson & Sheppard.
note: Possession hand-off P0569 (A1 Savile Row bespoke tailoring)

label: Neapolitan Tailoring
defn: the soft tailoring school of Naples, with unpadded shoulders, spalla camicia sleeves and little or no lining, developed in the 20th century as the counterpart to Savile Row structure.

label: Western Silversmithing
defn: the hand-engraved silver of the American West since the 1920s, with overlay figures and gold trim on belt buckles, spurs, bits and conchos, above all rodeo trophy buckles.
see: G1-31 Colonial Andean Silverwork; G3-15 Navajo Silverwork.
note: Possession hand-off P0581 (A1 Western trophy-buckle silversmithing)

label: Chanderi
defn: the sheer silk and cotton handloom weaving of Chanderi in Madhya Pradesh, with small supplementary-weft butis and zari borders, for saris and dupattas.

label: Maheshwari
defn: the light silk-and-cotton handloom saris of Maheshwar on the Narmada, with reversible borders and chatai, eent and other geometric motifs, revived in the 18th century under Ahilyabai Holkar.

label: Mangalagiri
defn: the pit-loom cotton weaving of Mangalagiri in Andhra Pradesh, plain-bodied saris and fabrics with Nizam-pattern zari borders.

label: Tangaliya
defn: the weaving of the Dangasia community of Surendranagar in Saurashtra, Gujarat, in which extra yarn is twisted around the warp to make raised bead-like dots (dana) forming geometric figures on wool and cotton shawls.

label: Kasavu
defn: the handloom weaving of Kerala, off-white cotton saris and mundu with fine gold or silver zari borders, centred on Balaramapuram.

label: Kota Doria
defn: the open-check cotton-and-silk weaving of Kaithun near Kota in Rajasthan, whose square khat pattern makes a translucent cloth for saris.
note: Possession hand-off P0597 (A1 Kota Doria weaving)

label: Nishijin-ori
defn: the figured silk weaving of the Nishijin district of Kyoto, for the court and aristocracy since the Heian period and today chiefly obi and kimono cloth, in brocade, damask, tsuzure and gold-thread weaves.

label: Qipao
defn: the Chinese woman's close-fitting dress of the 1920s onward, cut in Shanghai and Hong Kong with Western darts on the Manchu robe, with piped edges and knotted pankou fastenings.
note: Possession hand-off P0605 (A1 Hong Kong and Shanghai qipao tailoring)

label: Acheik
defn: the Burmese tapestry-woven silk of Amarapura, its wave patterns made with up to a hundred small shuttles, for court and wedding longyi and htamein.
note: Possession hand-off P0607 (A1 Acheik silk weaving)

label: Khmer Silk Weaving
defn: the silk weaving of Cambodia for the sampot, above all the weft-ikat hol in uneven twill and the pictorial pidan hangings, with brocaded charobab: sampot hol, pidan.
see: H5-12 Indonesian Ikat; H3-15 Naga Motif Weaving in Lao Communities.
note: Possession hand-off P0608 (A1 Khmer silk weaving)

label: Nyonya Kebaya
defn: the embroidered voile kebaya of Peranakan women of Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia, worked in machine and hand sulam with flowers and birds and fastened with linked kerongsang brooches.
note: Possession hand-off P0610 (A1 Peranakan nyonya kebaya embroidery)

label: Moroccan Caftan
defn: the ceremonial caftan and two-piece takchita of Moroccan women, tailored with sfifa braid and akaad knotted buttons and embroidered in silk and gold thread (UNESCO 2025).

label: Tlemcen Wedding Costume
defn: the bridal costume of Tlemcen in western Algeria, the chedda of velvet gold-embroidered caftan, conical crown and pearl jewellery, with the craftsmanship of its making (UNESCO 2012).
note: Possession hand-off P0612 (A1 Tlemcen wedding costume)

label: Majboud Embroidery
defn: the raised gold and silver thread embroidery of Algiers and other Algerian cities, couched over card or padding on velvet for the karakou, caftan and bridal furnishings.
note: Possession hand-off P0613 (A1 Algerian majboud embroidery)

label: Hausa Embroidery
defn: the hand embroidery of the robes (babban riga) of the Hausa aristocracy of Kano and Zaria, worked by men in silk or cotton on strip-woven cloth with the aska biyu (two knives) and spiral motifs.
note: Possession hand-off P0616 (A1 Hausa robe embroidery)

label: Shemma
defn: the Ethiopian narrow-loom weaving of hand-spun cotton by men of the highlands, with woven tilet and tibeb borders, made into the netela, gabi and habesha kemis: Shiro Meda, Dorze weaving.

label: Highland Dress
defn: the dress of the Scottish Highlands and Isles worn as a curated national costume since the 18th century: belted plaid, kilt, sporran and plaid in tartan.
note: Possession hand-off P0619 (A1 Highland dress & tartan)

label: Oaxacan Textiles
defn: the backstrap-woven and embroidered textiles of the Indigenous peoples of Oaxaca, Mexico, distinct by community: Amuzgo huipiles of Xochistlahuaca, Chinantec huipiles of Ojitlán, Tehuantepec Zapotec dress.
note: Possession hand-off P0625 (A1 Oaxaca indigenous textiles)

label: Pollera
defn: the national dress of Panama from the Azuero Peninsula, a gala skirt and blouse of white cloth worked in zurcido, appliqué, cross-stitch and lace, with tembleque headpieces.
note: Possession hand-off P0626 (A1 Panamanian pollera making)

label: Shweshwe
defn: the indigo discharge-printed cotton of South Africa, roller-printed with small geometric and floral figures since the 19th century and taken into Basotho, Xhosa and Tswana dress.
see: H5-32 Blaudruck; H5-36 African Wax Prints; H7-13 Basotho Blanket.

label: Indian Ikat
defn: the single and double ikat of India other than Patan patola, tied and dyed in warp, weft or both before weaving: Pochampally ikat, telia rumal, Sambalpuri bandha.
see: H5-8 Patola; H5-12 Indonesian Ikat; H5-1 Central Asian Ikat.

label: Tartan
defn: the twill-woven wool cloth of Scotland patterned in crossing coloured stripes (setts), from Highland district tartans to the clan, dress and regimental setts recorded since the 19th century: Black Watch, Royal Stewart.
note: Possession hand-off P0640 (A1 Scottish tartan weaving)

label: Tweed
defn: the rough woollen twills and herringbones of Scotland and Ireland, dyed and spun with flecked colour and woven in named regional cloths: Harris Tweed, Donegal tweed.
note: Possession hand-off P0641 (A1 Harris tweed weaving)

label: Faso Dan Fani
defn: the strip-woven hand-spun cotton cloth of Burkina Faso, spun and dyed by women and woven in narrow bands on horizontal looms, promoted as national dress from 1983.
see: H3-26 Ivorian Loincloth Weaving; H3-23 Kente Cloth.
note: Possession hand-off P0643 (A1 Faso Dan Fani weaving)

label: Kanzashi
defn: Japanese hair ornaments of lacquered wood, tortoiseshell, metal and folded silk worn with traditional coiffures, from the Edo period to the present: tsumami kanzashi of folded silk squares, bira-bira, kushi combs.
see: D5-25 Japanese Dolls (Ningyō); I2-10 Japanese Lacquerware.

label: Wayuu Weaving
defn: the crocheted and loom-woven fibre work of Wayuu women of the Guajira Peninsula (Colombia and Venezuela), with named geometric kanaas designs: mochila (susu) bags, chinchorro hammocks.

label: Kiondo
defn: twined bags of sisal and other vegetable twine with leather trim made by Kikuyu, Kamba and Taita women of Kenya, patterned in dyed bands.

label: Chinese Carpet
defn: knotted-pile carpets of China from the 17th century: Ningxia and Baotou carpets for monasteries and court, pillar carpets, and the Peking and Tianjin export rugs with relief-clipped pile, including the Art Deco 'Nichols' rugs.
aliases: Chinese rug;Ningxia carpet;Peking rug;Tianjin rug;Nichols rug
see: H1-13 Tibetan Rug; H1-1 Persian Carpet.
note: Possession hand-off P0090 (B2 Chinese rug weaving)

label: Tibetan Rug
defn: pile rugs of Tibet woven with the looped Tibetan knot for sitting, sleeping, meditation and saddles, peaking in the 19th–early 20th century and revived by exile workshops in Nepal and India: khaden, tiger rugs, Wangden warp-faced-back rugs.
note: Possession hand-off P0091 (B2 Tibetan rug weaving)

label: Savonnerie Carpet
defn: knotted-pile carpets of the royal Savonnerie manufactory at Chaillot, Paris (1615–1825, then at the Gobelins), woven in the Turkish knot to court designs: the Grande Galerie carpets of the Louvre for Louis XIV.
see: H3-39 Gobelins Tapestry; H3-31 Aubusson Tapestry.
note: Possession hand-off P0095 (B2 French court carpet (Savonnerie))

label: Welsh Tapestry
defn: reversible double-cloth woollen blankets and bedspreads woven by the mills of Wales from the 19th century, in geometric and jacquard panel designs: Caernarfon pattern blankets of Trefriw and Melin Tregwynt.
see: H3-32 Täkänä; H3-33 Northern Vidzeme Double-Weave Blankets.
note: Possession hand-off P0109 (B2 Welsh tapestry weaving)

label: Trade Blankets
defn: wool blankets and robes woven by Euro-American mills for trade with Native American and First Nations peoples, from striped point blankets to the jacquard-woven designs adopted as prestige dress and gifts: Pendleton and Beacon blankets, the Chief Joseph pattern, Hudson's Bay point blankets.
aliases: Native American trade blanket;Indian trade blanket;Pendleton blanket;camp blanket
see: H2-10 Navajo Weaving; H2-12 Coast Salish Weaving.
note: Possession hand-off P0111 (B2 Native American trade blanket)

label: Peshtemal
defn: flat-woven cotton and linen bath wraps of the Ottoman hammam woven on hand looms in regional stripe and check patterns, at Buldan, Denizli and formerly Antioch.
see: H4-2 Ottoman Embroidery; H3-3 Ottoman Silk Textiles.

label: Irish Linen
defn: linen weaving of Ulster and Ireland from the 17th century, above all the jacquard-woven figured damask of Lisburn, Banbridge and Belfast for table linen.

label: Basque Linen
defn: striped linen of the French Basque Country and Béarn, first woven by itinerant weavers as mantes à bœufs for cattle and now as table and kitchen linen with seven coloured bands.
see: H3-57 Irish Linen; H3-35 Bezdan Damask.

label: Rajasthani Block Printing
defn: hand printing of cotton with carved wooden blocks by Chhipa printers near Jaipur since the 16th–17th century: Bagru dabu mud-resist prints on dark grounds, Sanganeri floral prints on white.
see: H5-5 Ajrakh; H5-3 Indian Chintz; H5-4 Kalamkari.
note: Possession hand-off P0119 (B2 Rajasthani hand block printing (Bagru and Sanganer))

label: Indiennes
defn: block- and copperplate-printed cottons made in France and Europe after Indian chintz from the 17th century, banned in France 1686–1759: Provençal indiennes of Marseille and Tarascon, toile de Jouy of the Oberkampf manufactory.
aliases: indienne;Provençal prints;indiennes de Marseille;European printed cottons

label: Crewelwork
defn: embroidery in two-ply worsted wool on linen or linen-cotton twill, English from the early 17th century and carried to colonial America, with tree-of-life, flowering-branch and fanciful animal designs for bed hangings and curtains: Jacobean bed hangings, Deerfield crewelwork.

label: Hanji
defn: Korean handmade paper of paper-mulberry bark formed on the we bal mould and pounded (dochim) since the Goryeo period, and the crafts made of it: jiseung paper-cord weaving, jeonji coloured-paper boxes.

label: Thanjavur Dolls
defn: moulded and painted clay and papier-mâché dolls of Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu, notably the thalaiyatti bommai with a balanced nodding head, displayed in Navaratri golu.
aliases: Thanjavur thalaiyatti bommai;Tanjore dolls;Thanjavur dancing dolls
see: I1-7 Kondapalli Toys; I2-4 Channapatna Toys; A6-4 Tanjore Painting.

label: Stumpwork
defn: English raised embroidery of c. 1650–1700 with padded and wire-supported figures, worked by girls on satin for pictures, mirror frames and caskets.

label: Berlin Wool Work
defn: needlepoint in tent and cross stitch with bright wool on canvas, worked from hand-coloured charts first printed in Berlin (1804), the dominant domestic embroidery of Europe and America until c. 1875.
note: Possession hand-off P0404 (F2 Berlin wool work)

label: Jutti
defn: embroidered leather slip-on shoes of Punjab with straight lasts and upturned toes, worked in silk, gold and silver thread (tilla): tilla jutti, Patiala jutti, mojari, khussa.

label: Skep
defn: coiled-straw (earlier wicker) beehives sewn with bramble strips by skeppers of northern and western Europe and the British Isles, from the Middle Ages: straw skeps, skep caps.

label: Western Leatherwork
defn: the tooled, carved and silver-mounted leather of the vaquero and cowboy tradition, from Iberia and New Spain to the American West, Hawaii and the Great Basin: vaquero saddles, Sheridan-style floral carving, buckaroo gear, cowboy boots.

label: Moroccan Leatherwork
defn: vegetable-tanned leather of Fez and Marrakech cut, stitched and embroidered in silk and metal thread on poufs, slippers and bags: embroidered poufs, babouches.
see: H4-82 Tatar Leather Mosaic; C3-1 Islamic Bookbinding.

label: Shaker Furniture
defn: the plain, finely made furniture of the Shaker communities of New England, New York and Kentucky in the 19th century: ladder-back and rocking chairs, trestle tables, peg rails, oval boxes.

label: Chinese Classical Furniture
defn: hardwood furniture of China in huanghuali, zitan and other woods, joined without glue or nails, plain under the Ming and heavier and carved under the Qing: painting tables, horseshoe armchairs, recessed-leg tables.
aliases: Ming furniture;Ming and Qing hardwood furniture;huanghuali furniture
note: Possession hand-off P0071 (B1 Ming and Qing hardwood furniture)

label: Essaouira Thuya Marquetry
defn: inlay and marquetry in thuya burl of the workshops of Essaouira in Morocco, with lemonwood, ebony and mother-of-pearl tapped flush into the burl: boxes, trays, panels.
note: Possession hand-off P0073 (B1 Essaouira thuya marquetry)

label: Kashmir Walnut Wood Carving
defn: deep relief, undercut and openwork carving in walnut of Kashmir, with chinar leaf, lotus and vine designs on furniture, screens and boxes (GI 2008).
aliases: Kashmiri woodcarving;walnut wood carving of Kashmir
note: Possession hand-off P0074 (B1 Kashmir walnut wood carving)

label: Jepara Wood Carving
defn: relief and pierced carving in teak of Jepara in Central Java, from the 16th-century panels of the Mantingan Mosque to carved furniture and screens.
note: Possession hand-off P0075 (B1 Jepara wood carving)

label: Tansu
defn: Japanese mobile chests of the Edo and Meiji periods with forged iron hardware and lacquer finishes, in regional and functional types: isho-dansu, kaidan-dansu, funa-dansu, Sendai tansu.

label: Bandaji
defn: Korean drop-front storage chests of the Joseon period, read by region from their cut-metal fittings: Ganghwa, Kaesong and Namhansanseong bandaji.

label: Erzgebirge Folk Art
defn: turned, ring-turned and carved painted wooden figures and Christmas pieces of the Ore Mountains around Seiffen since the late 17th century: nutcrackers, smoking men, Christmas pyramids, candle arches.
see: D5-104 Wooden Toys of Hrvatsko Zagorje.

label: Dala Horse
defn: carved pine horses of Dalarna painted in kurbits style, made in Nusnäs since the 19th century and a Swedish emblem since 1939.
see: D5-104 Wooden Toys of Hrvatsko Zagorje.

label: Magewappa
defn: steam-bent boxes of straight-grained Akita cedar from Ōdate, stitched with cherry bark, made since the Edo period (designated traditional craft 1980).

label: Nantucket Lightship Baskets
defn: rattan-and-cane baskets woven over wooden moulds with solid turned bases, first by keepers of the Nantucket lightships in the 19th century, later lidded purses with carved ivory and scrimshaw.
note: Possession hand-off P0226 (C4 Nantucket lightship baskets)

label: Punch and Judy
defn: carved and painted glove puppets of the English street and seaside show descended from the Neapolitan Pulcinella, from 1662: Punch, Judy, the Crocodile, Joey the Clown.
note: Possession hand-off P0264 (E1 Punch and Judy)

label: Czech Marionettes
defn: string marionettes of the travelling family theatres of Bohemia from the late 18th century, carved by village church sculptors (UNESCO 2016 with Slovakia): Kašpárek, Matěj Kopecký's figures.
note: Possession hand-off P0265 (E1 Czech marionette puppetry)

label: Romanesque Ivories
defn: walrus-ivory, whalebone and elephant-ivory carving of northern Europe, 11th-12th century, from English and Scandinavian (Trondheim) workshops: Lewis chessmen, Bury St Edmunds Cross, Gloucester Candlestick.
see: D2-8 Byzantine Ivories; D2-11 Gothic Ivories.
note: Possession hand-off P0270 (E1 Norse walrus-ivory chessmen)

label: Tendō Shōgi Koma
defn: shogi pieces of Tendō in Yamagata, written, carved or raised in lacquer in named calligraphic styles since the late Edo period (traditional craft 1996).
note: Possession hand-off P0272 (E1 Tendo shogi koma)

label: Spanish Guitar
defn: the classical and flamenco guitar as built by the Spanish workshops of Seville, Almería and Madrid from Antonio de Torres (19th century) and the Ramírez dynasty.
note: Possession hand-off P0289 (E3 Spanish guitar making)

label: Djembe
defn: goblet drums carved from a single log by Mande smiths (numu) of West Africa, rope-tuned, often with carved bases.

label: Mbira
defn: lamellophones of the Shona of Zimbabwe with forged keys on a hardwood soundboard set in a calabash resonator (UNESCO 2020): mbira dzavadzimu, nyunga nyunga.

label: Violin Making
defn: the European lutherie of the violin family, in named schools and centres from 16th-century Cremona (Amati, Stradivari, Guarneri; UNESCO 2012) to Mittenwald, Mirecourt and the Vogtland.
note: Possession hand-off P0299 (E3 Cremonese violin making)

label: Tanpura
defn: the long-necked drone lute of Indian classical music with a gourd resonator, made above all by the family workshops of Miraj since c. 1850, with the sitar.
note: Possession hand-off P0303 (E3 Miraj instrument making)

label: Saraswati Veena
defn: the 24-fret veena of Carnatic music with a resonator hollowed from jackwood, carved and painted, made in Thanjavur since the Nayak court (17th century; GI 2013).
note: Possession hand-off P0304 (E3 Thanjavur veena making)

label: Celtic Harp
defn: the harps of Gaelic Ireland, Scotland and Wales, from the carved willow wire-strung clàrsach (Trinity College, Queen Mary and Lamont harps) to the Welsh triple harp.
note: Possession hand-off P0305 (E3 Gaelic wire-strung harp)

label: Cimbalom
defn: the Central European hammered dulcimer, from folk instruments to József Schunda's concert cimbalom of 1874.

label: Santur
defn: the hammered box zither of Persian and Iraqi maqam music, often decorated with khatam inlay, borrowed into Hindustani music as the santoor.
note: Possession hand-off P0308 (E3 Persian and Iraqi santur)

label: Appalachian Dulcimer
defn: the fretted box zither of Scotch-Irish Appalachia from the early 19th century, with heart and scroll soundholes, revived from the 1950s.
note: Possession hand-off P0309 (E3 Appalachian dulcimer making)

label: Kantele
defn: the Finnish and Karelian plucked psaltery, carved from one piece and later built up, a national symbol tied to the Kalevala.

label: Koto
defn: the Japanese long zither of paulownia with movable bridges, from the court gakusō to the Edo koto of Yatsuhashi Kengyō, often decorated in maki-e.

label: Guzheng
defn: the Chinese long zither with movable bridges, in northern (Shandong, Henan) and southern (Chaozhou, Hakka, Zhejiang) schools.
note: Possession hand-off P0312 (E3 Chinese guzheng schools)

label: Erhu
defn: the two-string Chinese fiddle (huqin) with hardwood neck and python-skin sound box, made in Beijing, Shanghai and Suzhou.

label: Taus and Dilruba
defn: the bowed fretted lutes of Sikh gurmat music, the taus carved in the form of a peacock, from the 17th century.
note: Possession hand-off P0314 (E3 Sikh bowed strings)

label: Sarangi
defn: the bowed fiddle of Hindustani music carved from one block of tun wood, with gut and sympathetic strings.

label: Hardanger Fiddle
defn: the Norwegian fiddle with sympathetic strings, decorated with ink rosing, bone and mother-of-pearl inlay and carved heads, from 1651.

label: Nyckelharpa
defn: the Swedish keyed fiddle of Uppland, from the medieval moraharpa to the chromatic nyckelharpa of the 20th-century revival.

label: Accordion
defn: free-reed bellows instruments with decorated cases, from the Castelfidardo workshops founded by Paolo Soprani (1863) to the Saxon concertina and bandoneon.
note: Possession hand-off P0318 (E3 Castelfidardo accordion making)

label: Bagpipes
defn: bagpipes of the British Isles with turned bores and ivory, silver and horn mounts: Irish uilleann pipes, Great Highland bagpipe.

label: Gagaku Instruments
defn: the instruments of the Japanese court music, from the Shōsōin lutes and harps to the hichiriki, ryūteki and shō made today.
note: Possession hand-off P0322 (E3 Gagaku instrument making)

label: Mechanical Musical Instruments
defn: self-playing instruments in decorated cases and façades: Swiss cylinder music boxes of Geneva and Sainte-Croix, Dutch street organs.
note: Possession hand-off P0323 (E3 Swiss music-box making)

label: Brienz Woodcarving
defn: carving of Brienz in the Bernese Oberland after 1816, sold as 'Black Forest' carving: bears, chamois and Alpine animals, hall stands, clocks.

label: Val Gardena Woodcarving
defn: carving of the Val Gardena (Gröden) in South Tyrol since the 17th century, exporting painted and gilded saints, altars, nativity figures and toys.
note: Possession hand-off P0422 (F4 Val Gardena woodcarving)

label: Butsudan
defn: Japanese household Buddhist altars of lacquered and gilded wood with carving, metalwork and maki-e, in designated regional centres: Hikone, Kyō, Nagoya, Kanazawa, Yamagata butsudan.

label: Vardo
defn: the horse-drawn living wagons of British Romani Travellers from c. 1870, carved, painted with scrollwork and gilded, in named types: Reading, ledge, bow-top, Burton wagons.
note: Possession hand-off P0450 (G1 Romani wagon building and painting)

label: Danish Freehand Pipes
defn: free-form briar pipes carved to the grain, from Sixten Ivarsson's Copenhagen workshop in the 1950s and his pupils (Jess Chonowitsch, Lars Ivarsson).
